events.continuity_hook: Starts a new distributor-training episode after the Visalia plant-visit logistics are settled.
events.interaction_goal: Build a practical flight-and-hotel shortlist, compare airport versus downtown hotel trade-offs, and keep the demo-case handling question visible.
events.scenario_brief: A Northwest distributor asks Jonah to lead a Friday morning controls-and-membrane troubleshooting training at their Spokane office, with a municipal pump-station walk-through tentatively planned for Friday afternoon. He needs Bay Area flight options into Spokane that arrive Thursday with enough time to review slides, avoiding two-stop routing and keeping the departure later in the day if it still protects the early start. Hotel options should compare airport-area practicality against downtown restaurant access, with strong guest feedback, workable early-morning transportation, and room basics for a one-night work stay. The open item is whether the distributor can receive a small demo case or Jonah has to check it on the flight.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Spokane training plan after the afternoon site visit and shipping details become clearer.
events.interaction_goal: Narrow the outbound airport choice, decide whether to stay Friday night instead of returning late, and pick the hotel location that best fits the early training schedule.
events.scenario_brief: The distributor confirms the pump-station walk-through will happen Friday afternoon and may run until about 4:30, making a rushed Friday evening departure less appealing. They also confirm the demo case can ship directly to their office, so hotel receiving is no longer needed. Jonah wants to compare a Thursday afternoon SFO itinerary with one manageable connection against a slightly cheaper Oakland option with a longer layover, and he needs to decide between a better-rated downtown hotel and a simpler property closer to the distributor office.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Spokane distributor-training trip from comparison to booking after the travel pattern is settled.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the flights, hotel reservation, room notes, seat selections, and concise two-night work itinerary.
events.scenario_brief: Jonah chooses the Thursday afternoon SFO-to-Spokane itinerary with one connection, stays over Friday night after the pump-station visit, and returns Saturday morning rather than cutting the workday short. He selects the downtown hotel because its stronger guest feedback and easier dinner options outweigh the longer morning ride to the distributor office. The booking needs a room note requesting a coffee maker and mini-fridge, plus window seats where seat selection is available.

events.continuity_hook: Adds a final access-and-arrival check to the already booked Spokane distributor-training trip.
events.interaction_goal: Update the itinerary with the new entrance, badge window, and demo-case instructions, then verify the practical hotel and flight details remain in place.
events.scenario_brief: A week before departure, the distributor sends a revised arrival packet with a different training-room entrance, a visitor badge pickup window, and instructions to bring the demo case through the service door rather than the main lobby. Jonah does not want to revisit flights or hotels; he only needs the itinerary notes corrected, the hotel-to-office morning timing checked, and the outbound seat assignment verified.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new client-site episode after the Spokane distributor-training trip is wrapped up.
events.interaction_goal: Create a flight, hotel, and rental-car shortlist that protects the Tuesday site schedule while leaving room for a possible Thursday add-on.
events.scenario_brief: A municipal utility outside Kansas City asks Jonah to attend a Tuesday pilot-media review and a Wednesday morning operations meeting at a treatment facility west of the city. He needs Monday Bay Area flight options into Kansas City that avoid awkward late arrivals and keep connections simple, plus a rental car because the plant is not convenient by rideshare. Hotel options should compare a suburban property closer to the plant against downtown hotels with better dining, while keeping guest feedback, parking, and early-workday room basics in view. The unresolved item is whether a distributor lunch on Thursday will be added, which would change the return date.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Kansas City utility visit after the schedule shortens but the Tuesday start becomes earlier.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the flights, rental car, suburban hotel booking, room request, and site-visit itinerary with the earlier Tuesday check-in highlighted.
events.scenario_brief: The utility confirms there will be no Thursday distributor lunch, but Tuesday site access moves earlier to a 7:00 a.m. visitor check-in. Jonah now wants to book a Monday afternoon Bay Area departure with one efficient connection, a Wednesday evening return after the operations meeting, a compact rental car, and the suburban hotel that shortens the early drive to the plant. The hotel should have solid guest feedback, parking, nearby dinner choices, and a room request for a coffee maker and mini-fridge.
